data.body:
Change pushed for review: https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/3121 (`91d39fd6061956c8d0a8a63489d6bf5de940df72`, hashtag `rebar-session-c657653d`). **`LLM-Review +1` on patch set 1**; `Verified` running (run 40516382656).

Local `make verify`: **19,840 passed, 88 skipped, 0 failed (46m16s)**. Git recorded the move as renames — 250 files touched, 118 insertions / 112 deletions — so `git log --follow` keeps pre-move history.

**On the one advisory (supply-chain, `codeql-config.yml`):** the finding says adding `evals/**` to `paths-ignore` "removes ~65 first-party executable Python files from static-analysis coverage". Those files were **not** under coverage before this change. The config's entire ignore list was `docs/**`, and the research tree lived at `docs/experiments/`, so CodeQL already skipped every one of them. Adding `evals/**` preserves that exclusion across the move; the net coverage delta is zero. Without it the change would have *added* 65 files to scanning — an unrelated and unreviewed expansion smuggled in by a directory rename, which is why the plan made this edit load-bearing rather than cosmetic.

The question the advisory gestures at — *should* developer-run research harnesses be CodeQL-scanned at all — is a real policy question, but it predates this change and is not resolvable inside it. Bounding the blast radius: the tree is confirmed non-shipping (wheel `packages = ["src/rebar"]` at `pyproject.toml:367`, sdist `include` at `:391`, no `MANIFEST.in`, and this change's ACs assert zero `evals/` entries in both artefacts), so any defect there reaches a developer running a harness locally, never a consumer of the package.

Not re-pushing for an advisory: a new patch set would mark the live `LLM-Review +1` and the in-flight `Verified` Outdated and re-queue CI.
